guidance: Take both stations from the same survey run and keep the station interval consistent with the rest of the trajectory, because the severity is an average over the interval and changes when the stations move. Enter the measured depth in the unit selected above the form; inclination is from vertical and azimuth clockwise from north. Read the result as the turn between the two stations only, and check it against the well plan and the bottom-hole assembly's stated build rate before acting on it.
method: The minimum curvature method treats the wellbore between two survey stations as a circular arc. With inclinations I1 and I2 and azimuths A1 and A2 in radians, the dogleg angle is beta = 2 arcsin sqrt(sin squared((I2 - I1)/2) + sin I1 sin I2 sin squared((A2 - A1)/2)), which is the same as arccos(cos I1 cos I2 + sin I1 sin I2 cos(A2 - A1)); the ratio factor is RF = (2 / beta) tan(beta / 2), taken as 1 when beta is zero, and the coordinate increments over a course length L are TVD = (L/2)(cos I1 + cos I2) RF, north = (L/2)(sin I1 cos A1 + sin I2 cos A2) RF and east = (L/2)(sin I1 sin A1 + sin I2 sin A2) RF. Dogleg severity is beta in degrees times 30 divided by the course length in metres, and beta times 100 divided by the course length in feet; the two reference lengths differ, 30 m against 30.48 m, so the two figures are not the same number scaled. Closure is the square root of north squared plus east squared and its direction is atan2(east, north) normalised to 0-360. Depths are accepted from 0 to 100,000 in metres or feet with a course length of at least 0.1, inclinations from 0 to 180 degrees, azimuths from 0 to 360 degrees (360 is read as 0), and two stations pointing exactly opposite each other are refused because the connecting arc is undefined. Warnings appear when both stations are within 1 degree of vertical (the azimuths carry no direction), when the severity exceeds 3 degrees per 30 m, when the interval is longer than the reference length (the value is then an average over the whole interval), and when the interval is shorter than 3 m (survey accuracy dominates). The page reduces one interval at a time and does not correct for magnetic declination or grid convergence, does not average or smooth a multi-station survey, and makes no judgement about survey quality, well-plan compliance or drill-string limits.

sources.title: Billger and McLeod, A technical note on dogleg severity, Coring Magazine issue 18: the minimum curvature method as the industry standard, the definition of dogleg severity in degrees per 30 m or 100 ft, and the Zaremba and Sawaryn references behind it.
